'''''Zygopetalum maculatum''''' is a species of [[orchid]] native to [[Peru]], [[Bolivia]] and [[Brazil]]. The plants are mainly situated in flat, very wet, moss-covered, semi-boggy areas at elevations of {{convert|1100 to 2500|m|abbr=on}}.<ref>http://www.orchidspecies.com/zygmaculatum.htm Orchid Species</ref>

==Description==
''Zygopetalum maculatum'' has a {{convert|40|cm|abbr=on}} long [[inflorescence]] with eight to twelve fragrant flowers. The flowers are {{convert|4-8|cm|abbr=on}} wide, and are green with red-brown markings with a white lip marked with violet.<ref>{{cite book |title= The New Encyclopedia of Orchids: 1500 Species in Cultivation |author= I. F. La Croix |edition= illustrated |publisher= Timber Press |year= 2008 |isbn= 9780881928761 |page= 497}}</ref>

Successfully pollinated flowers close slightly to indicate pollination. Pollinated flowers remain healthy and colorful for up to three months, but unpollinated flowers wilt after one month.<ref>{{cite book |page= 215 |title= Orchids of Tropical America: An Introduction and Guide |author= Joe E. Meisel |author2= Ronald S. Kaufmann |author3= Franco Pupulin |publisher= Cornell University Press |year= 2014 |isbn= 9780801454929}}</ref>
